definitions.explanation: moving up to a higher position, rank, or status
raising something to a higher category or level

examples.japanese: {課長|かちょう}に{昇格|しょうかく}した。
examples.english: I was promoted to section chief.

examples.japanese: {昇格|しょうかく}{試験|しけん}に{合格|ごうかく}した。
{彼|かれ}は{努力|どりょく}が{認|みと}められて{昇格|しょうかく}した。
examples.english: His efforts were recognized and he was promoted.

examples.japanese: チームが{一部|いちぶ}リーグに{昇格|しょうかく}した。
examples.english: The team was promoted to the first division.

examples.japanese: {支店|してん}から{本店|ほんてん}に{昇格|しょうかく}した。
examples.english: It was upgraded from a branch to the main office.

examples.japanese: {祝日|しゅくじつ}に{昇格|しょうかく}した{記念日|きねんび}がある。
examples.english: There are commemorative days that were elevated to national holidays.

notes:
FORMATION:
{昇|しょう} (rise, ascend) + {格|かく} (rank, status) → rise in rank

VERB FORM:
{昇格|しょうかく}する (to be promoted, to be elevated)

ANTONYM:
{降格|こうかく} (demotion)

RELATED WORDS:
- {昇進|しょうしん} (promotion - similar, focuses on position)
- {出世|しゅっせ} (advancement, success)
- {昇給|しょうきゅう} (pay raise)
- {格上|かくう}げ (upgrading)

DISTINCTION:
{昇格|しょうかく} emphasizes the change in rank or status category, while {昇進|しょうしん} focuses more on moving to a higher position. {昇格|しょうかく} is also used for non-personal things like teams or institutions.
